editorial.headline: The Waterway Work That Keeps Maritime Routes Functioning
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans navigation, waterways and specialised vessel support, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali PMA block under the recorded moratorium.
editorial.body:
Waterway support is the practical substance of this activity: services that enable vessels to navigate, sail and berth, rather than the movement of goods itself. Its field includes navigation and shipping services, lighthouse activity, the operation of waterways and related routes, and river-route information. It also reaches the transfer of cargo between large and small vessels, ship-cargo surveys, winter storage of vessels and maintenance work on waterway infrastructure. The scope further expressly includes operating floating production, storage and offloading vessels and floating storage and offloading vessels, rental of marine transport equipment or related-service equipment, and underwater work.

That breadth does not make every maritime undertaking part of the same activity. The stated perimeter excludes construction and dredging of waterways; construction of underwater cables or pipelines; cargo handling through loading and unloading; recreational or tourist marina-berth operations; and ship-crew recruitment services. The focus is instead on the operational services expressly named: keeping water routes functional, providing information and navigation-related support, conducting specified surveys and transfers, or carrying out the other listed work.

The code is open to registration at every listed enterprise scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. This is not a partial foreign-share arrangement. The recorded ceiling permits foreign investors to hold up to the entire stake nationally for this activity. That national position is tied to the stated source, Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse this national position through the island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium recorded here. That measure blocks all activities classified Low or Medium-Low risk for PMA. This activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and its stated OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali result is direct: it is not blocked by the moratorium. For a foreign-owned structure, the Bali picture is therefore not a concealed local prohibition but continued availability for PMA registration, with its higher-risk standing at the Besar scale explaining why the moratorium does not close it.
